steps.say: Speech marks show the exact words that someone says. They look like little 66 and 99 shapes.
Open the speech marks before the first spoken word. Close them after the last one.
The first spoken word starts with a capital letter.
The punctuation for the speech goes inside the speech marks. Use a comma, a question mark or an exclamation mark.
You can say who is speaking before or after the spoken words.

check.prompt: Which sentence uses speech marks correctly?

options.why: Said Lena is not spoken, so it goes outside.
All of Lena's words go inside the speech marks.
Ready is spoken too, so it belongs inside.

hints: What exact words did Lena say?
Only the spoken words go inside the speech marks.
Check that said Lena is outside them.
check.explanation: Lena said I am ready, so those words go inside the speech marks, with the comma.

check.prompt:
Which word needs a capital letter?
Rani said, “look at the moon.”

options.why: Said is in the middle of the sentence.
At is in the middle of what Rani says.
Moon is in the middle of what Rani says.

hints: Which word comes first inside them?
The first spoken word always starts with a capital.
check.explanation: Look is the first spoken word, so it needs a capital letter: “Look at the moon.”
